test_title: PYST 74: RRB Group D - GA (Held On: 30 Dec, 2025 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: In March 2025, the Disaster Management (Amendment) Bill 2024 was passed in the Lok Sabha. This bill seeks to amend which of the following Acts?
solution:
The correct answer is __**The Disaster Management Act, 2005**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Disaster Management (Amendment) Bill, 2024** was introduced in the **Lok Sabha** on **August 1, 2024**, and subsequently passed in **March 2025** to amend the **Disaster Management Act, 2005**.
 
• The primary objective of the amendment is to bring more **clarity and convergence** in the roles of various authorities working in the field of disaster management at the **National** and **State** levels.
 
• One of the significant features of the Bill is the establishment of a **National Disaster Database**, which will be maintained at the national level to store critical information related to disaster risks and mitigation.
 
• The Bill provides for the constitution of **Urban Disaster Management Authorities** in state capitals and large cities with **Municipal Corporations**, acknowledging the unique challenges of urban flooding and infrastructure risks.
 
• It grants **statutory recognition** to existing bodies such as the **National Disaster Response Force (NDRF)** and the **State Disaster Response Force (SDRF)**, formalizing their roles and responsibilities within the legal framework.
 
• The amendment empowers the **Central Government** to make regulations concerning the **Disaster Management** framework, ensuring a more flexible and responsive system to modern-day calamities. ***Hence, the correct answer is The Disaster Management Act, 2005.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Disaster Management Act, 2005**:
 
 
• This Act was enacted by the **Parliament of India** on **December 23, 2005**, following the devastating **2004 Indian Ocean Tsunami**.
 
• It established a three-tier structure: the **National Disaster Management Authority (NDMA)** at the center, the **State Disaster Management Authority (SDMA)** at the state level, and the **District Disaster Management Authority (DDMA)** at the district level.
 
• The **Prime Minister of India** serves as the ex-officio **Chairperson** of the **NDMA**, while the **Chief Ministers** lead the respective **SDMAs**.
 
 
 
• **Epidemic Diseases Act, 1897**:
 
 
• This is a colonial-era law meant to provide for the better prevention of the spread of dangerous epidemic diseases. It was widely invoked during the **COVID-19 pandemic** in **2020**.
 
 
 
• **Environmental Protection Act, 1986**:
 
 
• Enacted in the wake of the **Bhopal Gas Tragedy**, this Act empowers the **Central Government** to protect and improve environmental quality and control pollution.
 
 
 
• **National Green Tribunal Act, 2010**:
 
 
• This Act enabled the creation of the **National Green Tribunal (NGT)** for the effective and expeditious disposal of cases relating to **environmental protection** and conservation of forests.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Key Revisions in 2024 Bill**:
 
 
• The **2024 Bill** seeks to address the "overlapping" of functions between the **NDMA** and various ministries, ensuring that the **National Plan** is more comprehensive.
 
• It introduces provisions for **financial penalties** for individuals or organizations that fail to comply with the directions issued by the **Central** or **State Governments** regarding disaster management.
 
• The creation of the **National Disaster Database** is expected to help in **evidence-based decision-making** by tracking the **allocation and utilization** of funds from the **National Disaster Response Fund**.
